description: ACCEPT-tier records from Track 2 triage pipeline, ready for Article Finder full extraction.

records.title: Effect of daylight exposure on sustained attention in open-plan offices: a randomized crossover study
records.abstract: This randomized crossover trial examined sustained attention performance among 48 knowledge workers in an open-plan office across three lighting conditions. Workers exposed to natural daylight ≥150 lux showed significantly lower lapse rates (p<.001) compared to electric-only conditions, controlling for circadian phase.

records.title: Daylighting quality metrics and worker cognitive performance: a longitudinal field study
records.abstract: Nine-month field study of 120 knowledge workers correlating continuous illuminance monitoring with weekly cognitive assessments. Spatial daylight autonomy above 50% associated with 12% faster executive function performance.

records.title: Biophilic classroom design and student cognitive engagement: a quasi-experimental study in higher education
records.abstract: Quasi-experimental comparison of two university classrooms differing only in biophilic elements. Students in the biophilic classroom showed significantly lower perceived mental workload (p=.009) and 14% improvement on Stroop interference scores.

records.title: The effect of correlated colour temperature on reading fluency in secondary classrooms
records.abstract: Forty-two secondary school students tested under three CCT conditions (2700K, 4000K, 6500K). 4000K produced fastest reading fluency; 6500K supported best n-back performance. Findings suggest task-differentiated CCT recommendations.

records.title: Window-to-floor ratio and glare probability in knowledge-worker offices: a Monte Carlo simulation study
records.abstract: Monte Carlo simulations across 240 virtual office configurations. WFR >35% on south facades produces intolerable glare for >15% of occupied hours without shading. Cognitive alertness illuminance achievable at WFR 25-30% with appropriate shading.

records.title: Indoor plants and cognitive restoration in office workers: a preregistered field experiment
records.abstract: Preregistered 8-week field experiment with 96 office workers in three plant density conditions. High plant density produced significantly greater alerting network efficiency (p=.012) and lower afternoon cortisol (p=.028). Maintenance disruption effect was non-significant.

records.title: Dynamic lighting and cognitive fatigue in hospital nursing staff
records.abstract: 12-week parallel-group trial of circadian-tuned dynamic lighting for night-shift nurses. Dynamic lighting reduced end-of-shift fatigue by 1.4 points (p<.001) and improved N-back accuracy by 6% (p=.018). Habituation was not a significant moderator after 4 weeks.

records.title: Outdoor view content and attentional restoration in home-office workers during COVID-19 lockdown
records.abstract: Cross-sectional survey of 1,247 remote workers. Nature-content views predicted significantly higher Attentional Function Index (β=0.31, p<.001) and Perceived Restorativeness Scale (β=0.28, p<.001) after controlling for view distance, window size, and residential density.

records.title: Thermal preference and cognitive comfort in mixed-mode buildings: seasonal acclimatisation effects
records.abstract: Bi-weekly thermal comfort surveys and cognitive performance batteries (n=210 person-surveys, 14 months). Thermal preference alignment predicted higher working memory and processing speed (r=0.29, p<.001). Seasonal acclimatisation significant in summer but not winter.

records.title: Reverberation time and reading comprehension in open-plan primary classrooms
records.abstract: Multi-level regression across 48 classrooms (n=1,156 students). RT60 above 0.6s associated with 6.3 percentile-point decrease in reading scores (p=.003). Evidence-supported target: RT60 ≤0.4s for early literacy.
